title: The Edge of You Is Negotiable
evidence_boundary: The rubber-hand illusion, proprioceptive drift, and tool incorporation into the body schema are well-replicated findings. The outward extension to people and places is an interpretive metaphor, not a claim of identical neural mechanism.
desired_movement: From feeling the self as a fixed outline to seeing it as a live, updatable inference.
grounding: This is the same everyday machinery that lets you move without bumping into things; you are not an illusion.
invitation: What have you been treating as 'not me' whose seam you can no longer feel?
risk_mitigations: Ground the viewer and frame body-ownership as normal, healthy machinery.
Never claim the self is fake or an illusion.
Keep the outward extension explicitly metaphorical.
voice_standard: Liam — warm, sly, brilliant friend at midnight; conspiratorial on the hook, precise at the science boundary, hushed and weighty on the turn, grounded and sincere on the invitation.

scenes.text: That's the part worth sitting with. The edge of you was never a wall — it's a chalk line your brain redraws when the evidence changes.

scenes.text: It isn't magic. It's maintenance — your body-model updating second by second, so you can move through a world it only infers.

scenes.text: Maybe the edge of you was never where you thought. Maybe it's still being negotiated.
